subject: Private hosting architecture review — pick a deep-dive slot
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@altushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting architecture review — pick a deep-dive slot

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery: Altus is evaluating a private/VPC deployment for the inference stack (strict data residency, customer-managed KMS, and integration with your on-prem monitoring). You flagged three priorities: predictable latency under 50ms p95, encryption-at-rest/HSM for keys, and a minimal ops handoff for patching.

Next step I suggest is a focused architecture deep-dive with our infra and security leads to walk topology, NAAS requirements, and failure-mode handling. Can you confirm which of these windows works for your team (all times PT):

- Tue Jun 15, 10:00–11:00 (PT) — preferred by our infra lead
- Wed Jun 16, 14:00–15:00 (PT)
- Thu Jun 17, 08:00–09:00 (PT)

Please let me know who from Altus we should include (networking, security, cloud infra). I’ve attached a short discovery notes summary and a network checklist to help your ops team prep.

Prep asks for the call:
- DNS ranges and any existing peering/VPN topology (a redacted diagram is fine)
- Whether there’s a requirement for a private bastion or jump host
- KMS/HSM vendor info if applicable

Attachments: 2028-06-08-discovery-notes.pdf, priv-host-net-checklist.docx

If none of the slots work, tell me two alternatives and we’ll accommodate. I’ll loop in Marissa from our infra team once a slot is locked.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@altushealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Rivera <michael.rivera@altushealth.com>, engops@altushealth.com
Date: Fri, 8 Jun 2028 12:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private hosting architecture review — pick a deep-dive slot

Rishi — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist.

We can do Tue Jun 15 at 10:00 PT. Attendees on our side: myself (IT Ops), Michael Rivera (Network Lead) and one of our security engineers (TBD, likely onboard by next week).

Quick question on agenda — can you split the session into 30 min topology/runbook review and 30 min network/peering checklist? That will help us have the right people for each segment. Also, will someone from your side cover compliance/KMS questions?

SARAH HAYES
Director, IT Operations
Altus Health
sarah.hayes@altushealth.com

Date: Sat, 9 Jun 2028 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting architecture review — pick a deep-dive slot

Sarah — great, thanks for confirming Jun 15 at 10:00 PT. I’ve gone ahead and booked the slot: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/ALT-2345-deepdive (invite sent).

Proposed 60-min agenda (we’ll keep to the split you suggested):
- 0–5 min: Introductions & objectives (Rishi)
- 5–35 min: Topology and deployment runbook (Marissa) — network ports, LB patterns, autoscaling expectations
- 35–55 min: Peering, VPN, and connectivity checklist (Marissa + Michael) — NAT/firewall rules, routes, ingress patterns, bastion options
- 55–60 min: Compliance & KMS Q&A (Neha) and next steps

Attachments: 2028-06-09-agenda-privdeepdive.pdf

Marissa will lead the technical walkthrough and take actions on runbook items; Neha will cover compliance/KMS/keys. Can you share a redacted network diagram and any existing peering docs before EOD Monday (Jun 13)? That will let Marissa prepare specific questions and reduce time in the call.

If it helps, we can record the session and share slides after.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Rishi — I’ll take the technical lead for the call and will prepare a checklist-driven runbook. I’ll also review any network diagrams you get from Altus; if Michael can drop the diagram in the Drive link you included that'd be ideal.

Two quick asks for prep:
- If Altus has a required maintenance window or change freeze policy, flag that so I can avoid suggested changes during that window.
- I’ll need an IAM contact or ticketing owner if they want us to test a sample peering in a staging VLAN.

I’ll assemble the slides and share them by EOD Mon (Jun 13).

—Marissa
